findings.summary: Three older tests from the archived test-release feature had the tags [AC:spec-4-1..3]; the implementer renamed them to [gate-base-1..3]. The Test changes section does not name this. The change is title-only (no assertion, input or count changes) and it is needed so trace maps spec-4-* only to this spec's tests. It weakens no check. Older [AC:spec-27-*]/[AC:spec-31-*] tags in the same file were left as they were and show as unknown tags; this is harmless but inconsistent. Decompose could name such retags in Test changes.
findings.assumption: A title-only retag that the "Tag each new test [AC:spec-4-<n>]" line needs counts as required, not as an undeclared weakening.

findings.summary: The old case "a gate in the scope section gives no gap" (old [AC:spec-4-3]) directly conflicts with acceptance bullet 2, which makes that a gap. The implementer moved the gate bullet into a ## Notes section, so the remaining claim (a gate outside acceptance and scope gives no gap) is still tested. The scope claim it gave up is now asserted the other way, more strongly, by [AC:spec-4-2]. This is required by bullet 2, so it is not blocking, but Test changes did not declare the edit to an existing case.
findings.assumption: Rule: block only an undeclared change that no line requires; bullet 2 requires this change.

findings.summary: Probe: prose with a chain token after the command now matches, for example "If it fails, run `pnpm verify` || ask the owner.", "We considered pnpm verify && friends but chose not to.", "Do not run pnpm verify && pnpm lint here" and a table row "| pnpm verify | the gate |". Each sentence names the gate literally. The matcher already flagged such mentions before this spec when a prose word or punctuation followed, so this adds no new class of false positive. A negated or table mention is the only case a user might call a false positive. The gap message tells the author to rewrite it.
findings.assumption: gate-in-spec is meant to flag any naming of the gate in these sections, as the base tests (e.g. "run pnpm verify.") show.

findings.summary: A top-level fenced line in the scope section matches only when it equals the gate exactly. So a fenced "pnpm verify && pnpm lint" is not found there, while the same text in a bullet or an indented fence in a bullet is found by namesCommand. This keeps the acceptance-side fenced rule ("the same match"), so it meets the spec. Consider namesCommand for fenced lines too.
findings.assumption: The spec's "same match" means the acceptance check's exact-line rule for fences.
